chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah, from Al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked him about the drinker, and he said: “As for a man from whom there occurred a slip, then I would administer taʿzir to him. But as for another who persists habitually, then I would exhaust him with punishment, because he deems all sanctities lawful; and if the people and that were left alone, they would become corrupted.”

So this report is anomalous and rare; it is not permissible to act upon it because it conflicts with all the reports. Moreover, in the apparent wording of the report there is nothing more than that he asked him about the drinker, and he did not clarify to him whether he was a drinker of khamr, nabidh, or another drink; and it is possible that this ruling is specific to one who drank some of the forbidden beverages even if it was not intoxicating.

And that which clarifies what we have mentioned—that the ruling of nabidh in its small amount is the ruling of its large amount, and that its ruling is equal to the ruling of khamr—is what has been narrated:

key_terms.اَلشَّارِبِ: the drinker; the person consuming the prohibited beverage
key_terms.اَلنَّبِيذِ: nabidh; a beverage whose legal ruling is under discussion here
key_terms.اَلْحُرُمَاتِ: the sanctities or prohibitions made inviolable
key_terms.اَلْخَمْرِ: khamr; intoxicating wine, used here as the benchmark legal category
key_terms.زَلَّةٌ: a slip or isolated lapse into wrongdoing
key_terms.شَاذٌّ: anomalous; a report that departs from the established body of reports
key_terms.مُعَزِّرُهُ: one upon whom taʿzir punishment is administered
key_terms.يُدْمِنُ: persists habitually or repeatedly engages in drinking

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith distinguish between a one-time drinker and a habitual drinker, and what is the ruling on acting upon it?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the legal treatment of one who drinks a forbidden beverage, distinguishing between an isolated lapse and habitual persistence. It then states that the report is anomalous and cannot be acted upon as it stands, while suggesting that it may concern certain forbidden drinks, and affirms that nabidh shares the same ruling as khamr whether in small or large amounts.
